title: A modular simulation package for fed-batch fermentation: penicillin production
equations_quote: The extended model we have developed consists of differential Eqs. (1), (3), (9)–(18) that are solved simultaneously.

model_assumptions.text: Contois kinetics describe the dependence of specific growth rate on carbon and oxygen substrates.
model_assumptions.quote: The dependence of specific growth rate on carbon and oxygen substrates was assumed to follow Contois kinetics (Bajpai & Reuss) to consider the biomass inhibition.

model_assumptions.text: Substrate utilization is attributed to biomass growth and product formation, with constant yields and maintenance requirements.
model_assumptions.quote: The utilization of substrate is assumed to be caused by biomass growth and product formation with constant yields and maintenance requirements of the microorganism as suggested by Bajpai and Reuss (1980).

model_assumptions.text: The overall oxygen mass transfer coefficient depends on agitation power input and oxygen flow rate.
model_assumptions.quote: Here we have assumed  $ K_{la} $ to be a function of agitation power input  $ P_{w} $ and flow rate of oxygen  $ f_{g} $ as suggested by Bailey and Ollis (1986).

model_assumptions.text: The freezing and boiling temperatures used for the evaporation-rate expression are those of water; the exponent is taken as 5.
model_assumptions.quote: We have assumed that the evaporation rate will tend to infinity at the boiling point, and for engineering purposes the exponent 5 is large enough to represent this.

model_assumptions.text: The coefficient for the growth-associated heat term is constant.
model_assumptions.quote: where  $ r_{q_1} $ is assumed to be constant and might be treated as a yield coefficient (Nielsen & Villadsen, 1994).

model_assumptions.text: The heat exchanger is a cooling coil for a laboratory-scale fermentor.
model_assumptions.quote: A lab-scale fermentor was assumed in deciding to use a cooling coil, building the model, and developing the related equations.

model_assumptions.text: CO₂ evolution is attributed to growth, penicillin biosynthesis, and maintenance.
model_assumptions.quote: In this work,  $ CO_{2} $ evolution is assumed to be due to growth, penicillin biosynthesis and maintenance requirements as suggested by Montague, Morris, Wright, Aynsley and Ward (1986).
